item.text:
**7B.2 Research Note**

Bottom line: mostly no. In 2024 Hasina’s record is dominated by blame-shifting, coercive information control, and post-hoc cleanup rather than routine admission of error or correction of false claims. I found only weak counterevidence, and it is mostly after she had already lost power.

**Weak counterevidence**
- **US says it had no role in ousting of Bangladesh PM Hasina** | **The Straits Times / Reuters** | **August 13, 2024** | [link](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/us-says-it-had-no-role-in-ousting-of-bangladeshs-hasina) | The White House denied U.S. involvement, and the report says Hasina’s son said she never made the alleged “U.S. plot” statement. This only weakly rebuts one disputed accusation; it does not show Hasina herself corrected the claim. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1
- **Former Bangladesh PM Hasina demands probe into July killings and vandalism** | **Reuters** | **August 13, 2024** | [link](https://theprint.in/world/former-bangladesh-pm-hasina-demands-probe-into-july-killings-and-vandalism/2222256/) | After fleeing, Hasina called for an investigation into killings and vandalism. This is the closest accountability signal I found, but it is post-hoc and not evidence of admitting error while in office. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1, 1B.8

**Negative evidence**
- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | **Reuters** | **July 22, 2024** | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Hasina blamed political opponents for deadly protest violence and defended the curfew, which reads as blame-shifting and doubling down rather than owning mistakes. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1, 3B.3, 1B.8
- **Bangladesh shuts offices, imposes curfew to curb deadly job quota protests** | **Reuters** | **July 20, 2024** | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-studentled-protests-spiral-3527920) | Reuters reported a curfew, army deployment, and communications disruption as the government escalated. That is consistent with suppressing scrutiny, not allowing truthful reporting or correcting the record. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1, 1B.8
- **Bangladesh’s internet shutdown isolates citizens, disrupts business** | **Reuters** | **July 26, 2024** | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladeshs-internet-shutdown-isolates-citizens-disrupts-business-3539448) | The internet blackout cut off citizens and business activity during the crisis. That is strong evidence against a leader who allows truthful reporting and open scrutiny when facts are politically inconvenient. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1, 1B.8
- **The US and UK say Bangladesh’s elections extending Hasina’s rule were not credible** | **Associated Press** | **January 8, 2024** | [link](https://www.ksat.com/news/world/2024/01/09/the-us-and-uk-say-bangladeshs-elections-extending-hasinas-rule-were-not-credible/) | AP reported that key foreign partners viewed the election as not credible, free, or fair. That undercuts any claim that Hasina was candid about the legitimacy of the process that kept her in power. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1, 1B.8
- **Bangladesh repression: security force abuses discredit elections** | **Human Rights Watch** | **January 11, 2024** | [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) | HRW reported arrests for criticism and widespread repression before the election. This indicates the regime was punishing truth-tellers and suppressing dissent, not welcoming accurate reporting. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1, 1B.8
- **Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House said the Awami League manipulated the online information environment, blocked major news sites, and throttled communications around BNP rallies and later unrest. That is direct evidence of constraining truthful reporting. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1, 1B.8
- **Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House described harassment of the opposition and critical media, politicized institutions, and coercive control over state resources. This fits a pattern of misleading, deflecting, and pressuring critics rather than admitting error. | **QIDs:** 7B.2, 7B.1, 1B.8, 3B.3

**Search gap**
- I did not find a 2024 source showing Hasina herself publicly admitting an error, retracting a false claim, or materially correcting misinformation when correction would have protected her reputation or power.
- The only counterevidence is weak: one disputed attribution around a U.S.-role claim and one post-hoc probe request after she had already fled.
- I also found no strong evidence that she allowed truthful reporting during the major July crisis; the record instead points to shutdowns, arrests, and media pressure.
